hunks.baseline: Along with the hooves of horses racing across mountains and fields under the crack of whips, and the smoke of beacon fires staining the sky gray.
hunks.sol: On the hooves of horses racing across mountains and fields under the crack of whips, and in the smoke of beacon fires staining the sky gray.

hunks.baseline: Before the people shaken by the astonishing news could even determine whether it was true, they saw it with their own eyes.
hunks.sol: Before the people shaken by the news could even determine whether it was true, they saw it with their own eyes.

hunks.baseline: The moment they made out the five characters written on the flags, swollen full by the wind, they realized that denying it any longer would be no different from escaping reality.
hunks.sol: The moment they made out the five characters on those wind-swollen flags, they knew that denying it any longer would mean hiding from reality.

hunks.baseline: A mere band of river pirates, who had lived parasitically on the Yangtze with the world’s tacit consent, had at last risen to become its true rulers.
hunks.sol: A mere band of river pirates, who had lived off the Yangtze with the world’s tacit consent, had at last become its true rulers.

hunks.baseline: The groan that slipped between someone’s lips was hollow.
hunks.sol: The groan that slipped from someone’s lips sounded hollow.

hunks.baseline: After all, this vast empire, founded under the Mandate of Heaven, was collapsing.
hunks.sol: The vast empire founded under the Mandate of Heaven was collapsing.

hunks.baseline: More than a hundred years had passed since the age of warring heroes came to an end and a unified dynasty was born.
hunks.sol: More than a hundred years had passed since the age of warring heroes ended and a unified dynasty was born.

hunks.baseline: The country folk, who had held the Great Nation ruled by the Son of Heaven up as the heavens themselves, trembled with unease. The Confucian scholars groaned as they realized that the natural order had crumbled. The betrayed martial artists were swept up in anger and shock.
hunks.sol: The country folk, who had revered the Great Nation ruled by the Son of Heaven as heaven itself, trembled with unease. Confucian scholars groaned as they realized that the order they had taken for granted had crumbled. Betrayed martial artists seethed with anger and shock.

hunks.baseline: And on top of that, people belatedly realized that storm clouds were gathering beyond the distant Great Wall.
hunks.sol: And people belatedly realized that storm clouds were gathering beyond the distant Great Wall as well.

hunks.baseline: The news that the esoteric monks—counted among the Three Outer Powers alongside the North Sea Ice Palace and Nanman Beast Palace—had finally broken their long silence and stirred to action surprised no one in the Murim.
hunks.sol: The news that its esoteric monks—counted among the Three Outer Powers alongside the North Sea Ice Palace and Nanman Beast Palace—had finally broken their long silence surprised no one in the Murim.

hunks.baseline: In their eyes, as people of the Central Plains, Potala Palace had been nothing more than a pseudo-religion following evil doctrines since the distant past.
hunks.sol: To those firmly rooted in the Central Plains, Potala Palace had long been nothing more than a false sect following evil doctrines.

hunks.baseline: The New Murim Alliance had sent envoys to seek an alliance several times since its founding, but Potala Palace had always answered with silence. For them to act now, in a situation like this, could only mean one thing.
hunks.sol: Since its founding, the new Murim Alliance had sent envoys several times to seek an alliance, but Potala Palace had never answered. For it to act now could mean only one thing.

hunks.baseline: “...Dark Heaven. It’s them again.”
hunks.sol: “…Dark Heaven. It’s them again.”

hunks.baseline: Unlike the North Sea Ice Palace, which—as always—remained neutral, Nanman Beast Palace had overcome the threat of civil war thanks to the astonishing exploits of a young man and resolved to ally itself with the Murim Alliance.
hunks.sol: Unlike the North Sea Ice Palace, which remained neutral as always, Nanman Beast Palace had overcome the threat of civil war thanks to the astonishing exploits of a young man and resolved to ally itself with the Murim Alliance.

hunks.baseline: So the world’s attention focused on the Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance.
hunks.sol: So attention turned to the Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance.

hunks.baseline: The initial shock of learning the truth soon passed, and quite a few voices began to scoff at the dark-path forces’ uprising.
hunks.sol: The initial shock soon passed, and quite a few people began to scoff at the dark-path forces’ uprising.

hunks.baseline: “Even if they won one great victory, dark-path figures are still dark-path figures. Nothing’s changed.”
hunks.sol: “Even if they’ve won a great victory, dark-path figures are still dark-path figures. Nothing’s changed.”

hunks.baseline: The Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance together had nearly twenty thousand men, but if numbers alone could claim everything, the Beggars’ Sect would own the Murim world.
hunks.sol: The Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance together had nearly twenty thousand men, but if numbers alone were enough to take everything, the Murim world would belong to the Beggars’ Sect.

hunks.baseline: Everyone was confident that the orthodox factions, now completely united around the Murim Alliance, wouldn’t be shaken by a force this small.
hunks.sol: Everyone was confident that the orthodox factions, now united around the Murim Alliance, wouldn’t be shaken by a force of this size.

hunks.baseline: “Shaanxi has Huashan and Zhongnan, and Hubei has Wudang and the Zhuge Clan. And if the Imperial Army under the Son of Heaven moves out, those bastards will regret joining hands with Dark Heaven.”
hunks.sol: “Shaanxi has Huashan and Zhongnan, and Hubei has Wudang and the Zhuge Clan. If the Son of Heaven’s Imperial Army moves out too, those bastards will regret joining hands with Dark Heaven.”

hunks.baseline: But this prediction had a few fatal flaws.
hunks.sol: But that prediction had several fatal flaws.

hunks.baseline: Second, most of the hundreds of thousands of Imperial Army troops were concentrated in Jiangsu, where the Imperial Capital—home of the Son of Heaven—was located.
hunks.sol: Second, most of the hundreds of thousands of Imperial Army troops were concentrated in Jiangsu, where the Imperial Capital and the Son of Heaven were located.

hunks.baseline: And third, the Green Forest Alliance and the Yangtze River Channel League were marching west in broad daylight, with no thought of hiding themselves, and their forces were far larger than anyone had expected.
hunks.sol: Third, the Green Forest Alliance and the Yangtze River Channel League were advancing west in broad daylight, making no effort to hide, and their forces were far larger than anyone had expected.

hunks.baseline: Like a snowball slowly growing as it rolled down a snow-covered slope.
hunks.sol: Like a snowball growing as it rolled down a snowy slope.

hunks.baseline: “The Green Forest bandits gathered in Hubei crossed Tongsan half a shichen ago! Their numbers are estimated at around five thousand!”
hunks.sol: “The Green Forest bandits gathered in Hubei crossed Tongsan half a *shichen* ago! Their numbers are estimated at around five thousand!”

hunks.baseline: “Didn’t you say they were only around three thousand at most half a day ago?”
hunks.sol: “Weren’t there only around three thousand half a day ago?”

hunks.baseline: “W-Well, it seems the forces scattered among the various strongholds have joined them.”
hunks.sol: “W-Well, it seems men from the other strongholds have joined them.”

hunks.baseline: But the men who had so forcefully denied the messenger’s report soon learned the truth.
Another force had joined the two bands of outlaws who had secretly gathered around Hubei and Shaanxi even before the great battle in Gansu.
hunks.sol: But the men who so fiercely rejected the messenger’s report soon learned that another force had joined the two groups of outlaws secretly gathering around Hubei and Shaanxi since before the great battle in Gansu.

hunks.baseline: And they had done so by means of a certain method the Central Plains Murim had been most wary of.
hunks.sol: And it had reached them by the very means the Central Plains Murim feared most.

hunks.baseline: “...Damn it. They must have used that accursed dark art.”
hunks.sol: “…Damn it. They must have used that accursed dark art.”

hunks.baseline: “Dark art? Don’t tell me…”
hunks.sol: “Dark art? You don’t mean…”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. A Moving Formation.”
hunks.sol: “I do. A Moving Formation.”

hunks.baseline: The existence of the Moving Formation, once kept under the tightest security, was no longer a secret known only to a tiny handful.
hunks.sol: The existence of the Moving Formation had once been guarded with the strictest secrecy. Now it was no longer known to only a tiny handful of people.

hunks.baseline: As long as people had eyes and ears, secrets would always find a way to leak.
hunks.sol: As long as people had eyes and ears, secrets would eventually get out.

hunks.baseline: The Murim Alliance leadership and the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, led by the Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho, had taken the field, but for some reason, the secret of the Moving Formation had still gotten out. Now that they’d finally seen it for themselves, the Sect Leaders and Family Heads felt a chill.
hunks.sol: The Murim Alliance leadership and the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, led by the Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho, had taken the lead. Yet somehow, word of the Moving Formation had still spread. Now that the Sect Leaders and Family Heads had confirmation it was real, a chill ran through them.

hunks.baseline: Their Stronghold Lords commanded anywhere from a few dozen to several hundred, or even a thousand, men each. They pledged loyalty to their respective alliance leaders and repeatedly gathered and dispersed at their command.
hunks.sol: Their Stronghold Lords commanded anywhere from a few dozen to several hundred—even a thousand—men each. They pledged loyalty to their respective alliance leaders, gathering and dispersing at their command.

hunks.baseline: So the best time to strike them was right now.
hunks.sol: Now was the best time to strike.

hunks.baseline: Before the enemy had fully assembled. Before they had gathered in one place and formed a powerful force.
hunks.sol: Before the enemy had fully assembled. Before they could gather in one place and become a powerful force.

hunks.baseline: But the variable everyone had secretly feared had finally come to pass.
hunks.sol: But the complication everyone had secretly feared had come to pass.

hunks.baseline: No one knew where the Moving Formations were. And through them, Dark Heaven’s powerful forces were joining the dark-path figures.
hunks.sol: No one even knew where the Moving Formations were, and Dark Heaven’s powerful forces were using them to join the dark-path figures.

hunks.baseline: The Moving Formations themselves posed an enormous threat, and there was no guarantee they could win the battle.
hunks.sol: The Moving Formations alone posed an enormous threat, and there was no guarantee of victory.

hunks.baseline: Shaolin, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim. The Sichuan Tang Clan, one of the Five Great Families, with its deadly poisons and hidden weapons. Nanman Beast Palace and even the Hebei Peng Family had all suffered terrible losses.
hunks.sol: Shaolin, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, had suffered terrible losses. So had the Sichuan Tang Clan, which held its place among the Five Great Families with deadly poisons and hidden weapons. Even Nanman Beast Palace and the Hebei Peng Family had been badly hit.

hunks.baseline: That wasn’t all. According to reports, the Kongtong and Zhongnan Sects had also been hit hard in Gansu.
hunks.sol: And that wasn’t all. According to reports, Kongtong and Zhongnan had also suffered devastating losses in Gansu.

hunks.baseline: The damage was no less severe than during the Great Faction War, a time no one wanted to remember. If anything, it was worse.
hunks.sol: The damage rivaled that of the Great Faction War, a time no one wanted to remember. It might even be worse.

hunks.baseline: With even the fifteen great trees supporting the Murim world trembling at their roots in the typhoon stirred up by Dark Heaven’s storm clouds, it was no easy thing to summon the courage to risk everything and face the danger.
hunks.sol: Even those fifteen great trees supporting the Murim world were trembling at their roots in the storm stirred up by the dark clouds of Dark Heaven. Risking everything to face that danger took courage few could easily summon.

hunks.baseline: Especially for Sect Leaders and Family Heads, who were responsible for the lives of their families—not just their own.
hunks.sol: Least of all Sect Leaders and Family Heads, who were responsible for their dependents’ lives as well as their own.

hunks.baseline: “I… I give up.”
hunks.sol: “I… I’m withdrawing.”

hunks.baseline: “And you know that, yet…”
hunks.sol: “And you know that, yet…!”

hunks.baseline: “Please don’t call me that. I’m not worthy of it. I’m just a cowardly Sect Leader who wants to protect his family.”
hunks.sol: “Please don’t call me that. I’m not worthy of it. I’m just a cowardly Sect Leader who wants to keep his dependents safe.”

hunks.baseline: After muttering bitterly, he left. Several other Sect Leaders, their faces downcast, got up and followed him.
hunks.sol: He muttered the words bitterly and left. Several other Sect Leaders, their faces downcast, got up and followed him.

hunks.baseline: And so did the middle-aged man sitting quietly in the seat of honor, watching them.
hunks.sol: Then the refined-looking middle-aged man who had been watching quietly from the seat of honor rose too.

hunks.baseline: Scrape.
hunks.sol: *Scrape.*

hunks.baseline: The others wore complicated expressions—betrayal and anger, mixed with a sympathy that lingered in one corner of their hearts. At the sight of the middle-aged man getting up, their eyes widened.
hunks.sol: The others had watched the departing Sect Leaders with anger and a sense of betrayal, though part of them understood. Now their eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: They had firmly believed that even if everyone else left, he wouldn’t.
hunks.sol: They had been certain that even if everyone else left, this man wouldn’t.

hunks.baseline: But contrary to their ominous suspicions, the middle-aged man merely shrugged, his expression calm.
hunks.sol: But contrary to their fears, the middle-aged man merely shrugged, his expression calm.

hunks.baseline: The others relaxed, but let out a sigh at the same time.
hunks.sol: The others relaxed, then sighed.

hunks.baseline: A third of Hubei Murim’s leading figures had left. And he was going to get some air.
hunks.sol: A third of Hubei Murim’s leading figures had just left, and he was going to get some air?

hunks.baseline: It was certainly like him, but it was no less ridiculous.
hunks.sol: It was just like him. That didn’t make it any less ridiculous.

hunks.baseline: As the others stared at him in bewilderment, the middle-aged man clutched the front of his trousers, looking grave.
hunks.sol: As the others stared at him, the middle-aged man gripped the waistband of his trousers, looking grave.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know if it’s because I’m getting old, or because I’ve spent so long away from our family, living out in the world, but I think my bladder’s gotten weak. And on top of that, even when I’m just sitting still, a certain private spot on my backside starts tingling…”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know whether it’s age or all this time I’ve spent away from our family, living out in the world, but my bladder seems to have gotten weak. And even when I’m sitting still, a certain private spot on my backside starts tingling…”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man rambled on, then saw their expressions and smacked his lips.
hunks.sol: He rambled on until he noticed their expressions, then smacked his lips.

hunks.baseline: “Goodness, I shouldn’t have brought that up. Let’s continue where we left off.”
hunks.sol: “Well, I shouldn’t have brought it up. Let’s get back to our discussion.”

hunks.sol: “…Just go.”

hunks.sol: “No, no. I’ll wet myself right here. I’m sure even Zhuge Wuhou did when he was busy.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh? Then it’s all right if I do?”
hunks.sol: “Oh? Then you don’t mind?”

hunks.sol: “You’ve begged me so earnestly three times. I suppose I’ll have to follow the story of the Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage.”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man smiled at the half-resigned group. Then, Zhuge Feng, Family Head of the Zhuge Clan—or rather, the Crouching Dragon Guest—hurriedly left.
hunks.sol: Smiling at the half-resigned group, the middle-aged man—Zhuge Feng, the Crouching Dragon Guest and Family Head of the Zhuge Clan—hurried out.

hunks.baseline: He didn’t head for the privy. He walked for a long while through winding paths like a maze, until he reached the garden in the Inner Hall, a place only the Family Head was permitted to enter. At last, he stopped.
hunks.sol: He didn’t head for the privy. Instead, he wound through maze-like paths for some time before reaching the garden in the Inner Hall, where only the Family Head was permitted to enter. There he finally stopped.

hunks.baseline: “It’s all well and good to stay out of sight, but you should at least let me know where you’ll be.”
hunks.sol: “It’s all well and good to stay out of sight, but you should at least tell me where to find you.”

hunks.baseline: Zhuge Feng addressed the figure in a low voice.
